round18.ramp_finding: The World Bank Treasury's RAMP does NOT publish its membership. It only counts, and the counts conflict across World Bank pages: 'over 70' (2024 one-pager), '75th member' (April 2024), 'over 80' (May 2025), 'more than 90' (October 2025), 'a record 95' (April 2026). The only page naming members does so incidentally through seven staff profiles. All 14 RAMP ties this round were assembled one country at a time from individual World Bank press releases or the central bank's own announcement: GTM TTO KHM BGR ECU ZWE BIH ARM PRY XKX CPV LBR LBY SYC. Roughly 80 members remain unidentified; the same press-release search run year by year will keep yielding them. IMPORTANT: RAMP engagements differ in kind and each record says which. Most releases describe advice, technical assistance and training only. Seychelles is the one source found stating RAMP actually MANAGES a portfolio (US$100m from 2019), while the RAMP asset management page says the Treasury 'manages assets for all RAMP members, totaling over $30 billion' without naming a client. Do not upgrade membership or advice into management.

A second copy under /files/2024-01/ is 369 characters and fails identically. browser_round.method: Load pdf.js from cdnjs into an ordinary HTML page on the PDF's OWN origin, then getDocument(url) and walk the text layer. Where the text layer is empty the page is a scan: render that page to a canvas, replace the body with it, and screenshot. Chrome's own PDF viewer exposes no text to any reader, so navigating straight to the PDF is useless. Same origin matters - a cross-origin PDF is refused by CORS.
